tagline: A freeway plan became a parkway with fences and a footpath
intro: Split-rail fences, landscaping and a parallel multi-use trail give the US 202 Parkway its roadside character. Between PA 63 and PA 611, the road winds past development, fields and woods, changing from four lanes to two at PA 463. PennDOT lists it as a Scenic Byway under Act 140 of 2012. Billboards are prohibited along the route.

The parkway followed decades of unsuccessful freeway proposals. Environmental concerns, local opposition and development had blocked further expressway construction in Bucks and Montgomery counties. Funding cuts in 2005 changed the plan to a two- to four-lane parkway. Construction began in 2008, and traffic first used the completed road on December 3, 2012. The new alignment drew customers away from businesses on the old route; their campaign for a Business 202 designation won approval in 2015. The parkway also bears the name of George A. Penglase, a Bucks County business leader who pushed for a US 202 bypass.

From PA 63, head northeast past the PA 309 interchange and the narrowing at PA 463. Beyond County Line Road, fields and woods accompany the route into Bucks County. The Neshaminy Creek crossing comes next in Doylestown Township, followed by the approach to PA 611, where the parkway gives way to a freeway.
notice: Split-rail fences and landscaping line the parkway beside its multi-use trail.

moments.title: PA 309 interchange, Montgomeryville
moments.text: At PA 309, the parkway trail makes a loop of its own. It crosses beneath US 202 at the bridge, moves to the west side, then loops back to cross PA 309 on the same bridge as the parkway. This interchange lies south of Montgomeryville. Farther along, the road crosses the trail again at Costco Drive/Terrace Way before reaching PA 463, where four lanes narrow to two.

moments.title: Neshaminy Creek
moments.text: The parkway crosses Neshaminy Creek on the 1st Lt. Travis L. Manion Memorial Bridge in Doylestown Township. After Bristol Road, the parallel trail runs on the west side of US 202 as the road curves east toward the water. Beyond the bridge, fields and woods continue along the route, which turns northeast and passes over Almshouse Road.

moments.title: New Britain Road and the parkway’s end
moments.text: Near the end of the parkway, the road passes northwest of Doylestown Central Park and crosses over New Britain Road. The parallel US 202 Parkway Trail ends at that crossing. US 202 then becomes a four-lane freeway at the approach to PA 611. That Doylestown bypass belongs to an earlier construction campaign: work began in 1971 and the route was completed in 1976. Its ends were designed for an expressway that planners intended to extend in both directions. The bypass continues south of Doylestown through wooded land, with an interchange at South Main Street serving the borough.
